title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 45-47): Σ is the Riemann sphere and J = {R_i | i ∈ I} is a set of three points, the vertices of an equilateral triangle; the previous page mentions an equilateral triangle and symmetries. The aim is to compute the fundamental groupoid of Σ* = Σ − J as a preliminary exercise in 'synthèse galoisienne', before treating richer symmetric configurations and Teichmüller groupoids. For that he wants base points 'close to' the punctures R_i, so he compactifies Σ*.

On this page:
(1) Unoriented real blow-up. He takes the real blow-up Σ' of Σ at the R_i. The fibre over R_i is the real projective line Σ'_{R_i} = P(T_{Σ,R_i}) = (T_{Σ,R_i} − 0)/R*. This is a circle embedded in the compact surface Σ'. Topologically, Σ' is the sphere with three small discs removed and three Möbius bands glued in. It is non-orientable.
(2) Euler characteristic. Using the additive, compactly supported Euler characteristic χ_!:
- χ_!(Σ') = χ(S²) − 3·χ_!(open disc) + 3·χ_!(Möbius band, minus boundary as appropriate);
- this gives 2 − 3·1 + 3·0 = −1.
Writing χ = 1 − g, he concludes 'genus 2'.
(3) Oriented real blow-up. Cutting Σ' along the three exceptional circles gives a compact surface with boundary Σ̃. Its boundary is a double cover of ∐ Σ'_{R_i}. Concretely, ∂Σ̃ ≅ ∐_i U_i, where U_i = (T_{Σ,R_i} − 0)/R*_{>0} is the circle of tangent directions (unit tangent circle) at R_i. Thus Σ̃ is the real oriented blow-up of Σ at J, a sphere with three holes.
(4) Bottom margin. The interior Σ̃° ≅ Σ* carries a conformal structure, but it does not extend to Σ̃.
(5) Top margin (partly illegible). A remark that the construction of the real blow-up in the C^∞ category, for real-analytic incidence data (centres/divisors), deserves to be done (in his opinion).

Next page: Rev(Σ̃) ≃ Rev(Σ̃°) ≅ Rev(Σ*). Hence Π_1(Σ̃) ≃ Π_1(Σ*), and the boundary circles give maps Π_1(U_i) → Π_1(Σ*). Points of U_i thereby serve as base points 'infinitely close' to R_i, i.e. tangential base points, pictured via fictitious infinitesimal discs D_i.
errors: 'genre est 2' uses the convention χ = 1 − g for a non-orientable surface; g is then the genus of the orientation double cover (χ = −2). In the usual crosscap convention, Σ' (sphere with 3 crosscaps, ≅ torus # RP²) has non-orientable genus 3. This is a convention issue, not a real error.
The notation T^*_{Σ,R_i} in the brace means T_{Σ,R_i} − {0}, not the cotangent space; P(T) = (T−0)/R*.
The Euler characteristic bookkeeping is slightly loose about open versus closed Möbius bands and discs, but the result χ = −1 is correct: χ_c(Σ*) = −1, and the three added circles contribute 0.
'i ∈ J' should presumably be 'i ∈ I' (index set), with J the set of points R_i.

ideas.what: Real (unoriented) blow-up of a surface at points: exceptional fibre P(T_x) ≅ RP^1, producing a non-orientable surface (crosscaps)
Oriented real blow-up obtained by cutting along the exceptional circles; boundary = circles of tangent directions (T_x−0)/R_{>0}; compactification of Σ* homotopy-equivalent to it
ideas.modern_name: real oriented blow-up (A'Campo; Kato–Nakayama log space)

ideas.what: Using points of the boundary circles U_i as base points near the punctures, with Π_1(U_i) → Π_1(Σ*) (continued next page)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne 1989 (Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points); Ihara
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses fundamental groupoids with base points adapted to the boundary/Teichmüller tower, but I am unsure it uses tangential base points explicitly

ideas.what: Computing χ via additive compactly supported Euler characteristic χ_!

missed.claim: Grothendieck works out, in private notes dated from 1978 on, the oriented real blow-up with boundary circles = unit tangent circles at punctures, in order to have base points 'close' to the punctures for Galois-theoretic computations of fundamental groupoids. This is essentially the tangential base point formalism later made standard by Deligne (1989). It is a priority/historical detail rather than a new result.
missed.quote: ∂Σ̃ ≃ ∐_{i∈I} TU_{Σ,R_i} (cercle tangent à Σ en R_i, identifié à T*_{Σ,R_i}/R*+)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents Grothendieck's independent use of tangential base points in the anabelian/Teichmüller program, relevant to the history of Galois actions on π_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}).

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is standard: real blow-ups and boundary circles as tangential base points. The only interest is historical, namely an early use of tangential-type base points in Grothendieck's Galois–Teichmüller notes, already known in spirit from the Esquisse.
transcription_corrections: Bottom margin likely reads: 'Σ̃ est une sphère à bord à trois trous. Σ̃° est munie d'une structure conforme, mais celle-ci ne se prolonge pas à Σ̃'.

Above the χ_! formula, the term is '−3χ_!(rondelle ouverte)' with the value −3 indicated, and '3(χ_!(ruban Möbius))' with value 0 underneath. The crossed-out '+3' and the crossed-out word 'genre' before χ_! are correct.
In (11) and (12), T^* should be read as T − {0} (punctured tangent space), not the cotangent space.
'pts de J' / 'i ∈ J' is probably meant to index by I.
